name: eclipticam-v3w
resolution_notes: FULL-RES native IMX708 (4608x2592) — this is what the night daemon actually captures since 2026-06-22 (v3w_night_daemon sensor_size=(4608,2592)); was [2304,1296] binned. ⚠️ CALIBRATION-BASIS MISMATCH: pedestal, plate_scale_deg_px, and distortion k1/k2 below were all derived on the OLD BINNED geometry (2304x1296 / 1152x648 / 648) and have NOT been re-fitted to full-res. Until they are (see v3w_night_daemon.py comment): pedestal ~4x too high for full-res un-binned (binned sums 4 px); plate_scale is per-BINNED-px (full-res ≈ 0.02215 deg/px, half); distortion rho is normalised so scale-invariant but re-fit anyway on in-focus full-res. Do NOT trust the derived numbers as full-res without re-derivation.
pedestal_notes: CHART FLOOR ONLY — the reference for the log2(mean/pedestal) 'stops' axis, chosen for footroom, NOT a physical measurement. See black_level for the sensor's electronic zero and blackest_observed for the darkest sky recorded. Set to 50 to match astrocam so both cameras' charts share an axis. HISTORY: was 4380, which the old note called a 'BINNED-BASIS black level (2x2 sum)' ~4x too high for full-res — that explanation was WRONG. 4380 was simply the MSB-aligned form of ~68 (4380/64 = 68.4): the Pi 5 ISP left-shifts 10-bit raw by 6 bits, nothing to do with binning. Proof: after the 2026-08-20 repack the binned-era floor (75.64) and the full-res floor (71.29) differ by ~4 ADU, not the 4x a 2x2 sum would give. Superseded 2026-08-20.
black_level_notes: IMX708 sensor electronic zero in 10-bit LSB-aligned ADU — what a photosite reads with no photons. A property of the silicon, not a tuning knob. CONFIDENCE: INFERRED, not measured. Nominal 64 for IMX708, consistent with this camera's own earliest v3w floor of 64.82 (an upper bound: it includes minimum sky). NOT measured from dark frames. To settle it, cap the lens and take a master dark; that also tests whether it moves with analog gain, which matters before any gain bracketing. Same sensor as astrocam's v3s — the two should agree, and disagreement would be informative.
blackest_observed_notes: Darkest frame mean ever recorded, 10-bit LSB-aligned ADU, 2026-08-20, over n=18834 frames (mode imx708_full_59.9s, from 2026-06-25). FOOTROOM = blackest_observed - black_level = ~7.3 ADU: the entire clear-sky signal above the electronic floor sits in about seven integers, which is the real argument for gain bracketing (see the strand STATE.md). Astrocam reads ~19.8 on the same sensor — f/1.8 vs this f/2.2 wide lens accounts for 1.49x of that, pointing for the rest. Caveat: a min-of-N estimator, biased low as frames accumulate, so not comparable across cameras with different N. Refresh from the quality DB; do not hand-edit downward.
capture_notes: v3w NIGHT streaming-capture params — the single source of truth for eclipticam/v3w_night_daemon.py (it reads these; env vars V3W_EXPOSURE_US / V3W_GAIN / V3W_LENS_POSITION still override per-host). lens_position: IMX708 manual focus in dioptres; 0.0 ('nominal infinity') is badly soft on this Module 3 Wide — true infinity is ~3.15 (autofocus settled 3.07-3.25; rooftop sharpness ~10x better than 0.0; measured 2026-06-21). night_exposure_us ~60s at 1-min cadence. DAY focus is the same value but lives in eclipticam/capture.py LENS_POSITION_V3W (day uses rpicam-still, not this daemon) — keep the two in step until capture is unified. KEEP LENS POSITION FIXED: the Module 3 lens has FOCUS BREATHING (lens position changes effective focal length -> FOV/plate scale), so a single constant is required for calibrations to compose. Do NOT autofocus or vary focus for temperature. All calibration dated 2026-06-21 or earlier (k1/k2 distortion in the 'distortion' block, moon pointing, plate_scale_deg_px) was at the OLD lens=0.0 out-of-focus FOV and MUST be re-derived at 3.15 before use with in-focus frames.
plate_scale_notes: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-29 - DO NOT USE AS A CONSTANT. 0.0443 deg/px (159.5 arcsec/px binned, 79.74 full-res) is the FIELD AVERAGE, not a plate scale: it was derived as 102 deg / 2304 px, which treats a varying scale as constant. The star solve on night 2026-07-25 (15 probes, 5 stars, 5 epochs, rho 0.18-0.60, rms 1.61 px) gives a GNOMONIC projection about the optical axis with f = 1957.8 px: centre scale 105.4 arcsec/px falling as cos^2(theta) - 98 at Altair, ~70 at 35 deg off-axis, ~44 at the field edge. Averaging those lands on 79.7, which is where the old number came from. Horizontal FOV 99.3 deg (nominal 102). Use the projection in the "astrometry" block; a single arcsec/px figure carries a 10-20 percent systematic anywhere off centre.
rotate_180_notes: Camera sensor is physically mounted upside down. In-capture 180° rotation is applied during streaming capture (StreamingConfig rotation_180=True) and day stills (rpicam-still --rotation 180) so stored frames are right-side up (array-top = sky-top). No downstream rotation is applied in processing.

astrometry.note: Gnomonic (rectilinear) about the OPTICAL AXIS - not about the pole. The celestial pole is 95.1 deg off-axis and BEHIND the camera (this camera looks south), so pole-based derotation and splay's _epoch.reg rotate-about-pole overlay scheme do NOT apply here: measured error of rotate-about-pole is 1064 px after 10 min. De-TRANSLATION is the right operation for this camera; overlays must be per-frame. Solved from 15 star probes (Altair/Tarazed/Alshain/Enif/Skat) over 5 epochs on night 2026-07-25, rms 1.61 px, rho 0.18-0.60. Equivalent to the 2026-08-24 'equidistant + 0.42*theta^3' solve: tan x = x + x^3/3 + ..., and the best-fit cubic coefficient for tan over 0-50 deg is 0.440. CAVEAT: pointing is PER-NIGHT - the camera moves between nights (1.9 deg between 08-24 and 08-25), so az0/alt0/roll below are for 2026-07-25 only; f and the projection form should carry across. Corners (rho > 0.6) are still unprobed.

detrans_notes: De-translation (detrans) velocity for the registered-streak sweep deliverable (bin/detrans-sweep). The pole is far off-frame, so over a short window the star motion is a near-uniform translation; shift each frame by -v*(t-t0) along angle_deg to register the 60s streaks into one sharp high-SNR streak, then max-stack. v_frac_per_s is the RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT velocity as a fraction of image WIDTH per second (detrans-sweep scales it to px/s = v_frac * W at whatever working resolution/bin the run uses, so it survives the 2026-06-22 2304->4608 full-res switch). 3.4722e-5 width/s = the original 0.040 px/s fit on the BINNED 1152-wide geometry (0.040/1152). Angle 7.8deg (from horizontal). Found 2026-06-21: angle from the separated trail centrelines (median 7.8deg, tight IQR), speed refined visually from a 10-min window sweep (0.040 gave the shortest streaks; analytic equator rate is 0.047 px/s, so cos(dec)~0.85 -> dec~32deg, a sane consistency check). Independently cross-checked k1/k2 via corner-vs-centre streak registration. Applies AFTER undistortion (the velocity field is only uniform once the lens is removed).
distortion_notes: REFUTED 2026-08-29 - k1/k2 BELOW ARE NOT THE LENS. A gnomonic (rectilinear) projection with NO distortion term fits 15 star probes at rms 1.61 px over rho 0.18-0.60; adding a radial k1 buys 0.04 px and fits to k1 = -0.0049, i.e. 130x smaller than the -0.636 below. Under -0.636/+0.311 the same sky positions land 500-625 px away at the corners; two stars already decide it (Skat: models differ 295 px, gnomonic predicted 2 px from probe; Enif: 69 px apart, again 2 px). Independently, astrometry.net solved a 47x37 deg crop of this camera on a plain TAN with 38 matches and 0 conflicts, which a real barrel of that strength would not permit. LIKELY CAUSE: the 2026-06-21 fit minimised trail BOW only, but circles of constant declination are not great circles and project to genuinely curved conics even through a perfect gnomonic lens - so real sky curvature was absorbed into a spurious barrel term. It was also fitted at lens_position 0.0, out of focus, so it may describe a different optical configuration rather than being simply wrong. Historical fit follows. Radial distortion, r' = r*(1 + k1*rho^2 + k2*rho^4), rho = |p - centre| / R with R the HALF-DIAGONAL and centre the frame centre. k1 = -0.636, k2 = +0.311 fitted 2026-06-21 from the night-2026-06-20 max-stack: ~49 star-trail centrelines separated by a Hessian ridge crawler (bin/separate-trails, incl. corner trails out to rho~0.95), then (k1,k2) minimising total per-trail bow (the trails are near-straight chords because the celestial pole is far off-frame, so residual bow IS the lens). 'Barrel with an edge correction': k1 alone (-0.345) straightens the bulk excellently but leaves residual corner curvature (see edge.png, top-left); the +k2*rho^4 term bends the correction near the corner to match it. Displacement is monotonic barrel (-3px at rho 0.2 to -215px at the corner). Minimum is a real bowl (objective rises in all directions; soft along the k1<->k2 trade as expected), NOT degenerate. Confirmed visually in splay: 04_k1k2 corrects the corner that 03_k1only leaves bowed. Defined on BINNED 1152x648 geometry; rescale rho_norm/centre for full-res. Free-centre fit is degenerate on this data (centre runs to infinity) — needs more corner coverage; keep centre fixed. Alternative if k2 ever looks unreliable: crop to a valid radius (rho<~0.85, just inside the inner edge.png dot) and use k1 only. See bin/fit-distortion-trails and worklog 2026-06-21.
frames_root_notes: Single source of truth (CameraConfig.frames_root), resolved PER-HOST. Default (~/eclipticam-frames) is the capture host's view (muppet's bigstore export NFS-automounted there); pip reaches the same export at /mnt/muppet/bigstore/eclipticam-frames (pip's ~ symlink removed 2026-08-02). Add a host key to teach a new machine.
night_layout_notes: TRANSITIONAL: live v3w_uploader.py still writes to night/<night>/v3w/HH/<epoch_ms>.fits.fz. The post-split camera name 'eclipticam-v3w' resolves the legacy 'v3w' subcam via the percam reader. Once the uploader is migrated, flip to 'canonical' (per DECISIONS.md 2026-06-16): <frames_root>/YYYY/MM/DD/eclipticam-v3w/night/HH/HH-MM-SS.fits.fz. brightness.csv already lands at the canonical path (astro.brightness_log.append writes there directly).
sky_clear_max_stops_notes: Dark-trough brightness above which the night is called 'cloudy' and the chart draws the clear/cloudy line. v3w (16-bit container, pedestal 4380, ~13 stops of headroom) sits at +0..+6 stops on a clear dark trough; +10 is the empirical ceiling where stars stop being separable from cloud-glow. Per-sensor — astrocam uses a much lower value (see its camera.json). This was the global hardcoded default before 2026-06-21.
state_notes: Night starts when the sun is 10 deg below the horizon (was the -12 default) so night capture begins ~30-40 min earlier. Frame-quality gating still rejects too-bright twilight frames from the stack.
brightness_roi_notes: Frame-quality gating measures brightness over the top half of the frame only. A neighbour's ground-level lights low in the v3w frame raised whole-frame brightness enough to push a clear, starry night (2026-06-19) out of the stacking band -> wrongly verdict=cloudy. The sky (top half) is unaffected. v3w only; v1 has no ROI. The stack itself still uses the full frame. v3w is not rotate_180 so array-top = sky-top.
reference_nights_notes: Known dark/clear reference night always overlaid on the multi-night brightness chart (combined-brightness) as a fixed baseline. Plotted alongside the last 6 rolling nights (combined-brightness --recent default 6, raised from 3 on 2026-08-24 when the astrocam chart was reworked) for a 7-curve chart. The default is shared by every camera because publish-night-cam passes no --recent. 2026-07-25 is the chosen reference (Peter, 2026-08-25), replacing 2026-06-12. 06-12 scored a lower dark-trough (4.43 vs 4.47 stops) but is not usable as a baseline: its CSV runs 12:00->03:25 UTC and carries 98 saturated daytime frames, and it is one of the 9 MSB-aligned nights. 07-25 is LSB-native, clear, 338 frames over a full 5.6 h window (21:21->02:57 UTC), and within 0.04 stops of the darkest night in the archive. Drawn bold dashed.
